Case in point I have a blog I'd like people to read, can I drop links on Voat if they are relevant? What's going to be SPAM and what's not going to be SPAM. Question about promoting content on Voat.

Officially, I'm not sure what voat's policy is other than it's frowned upon and you can only cross-post the same link twice.

Personally, I think it depends on how it comes about and in which sub it's posted. I'd have no problem with people promoting their own stuff as long as it comes about organically. If someone is requesting help on learning powershell scripts and your blog has a write up on powershell then you should share it. I also think it can be good practice to let people know it is your own material so it doesn't look like you're trying to be sneaky. Now if you go about posting a link to your powershell blog in reply to multiple comments in a single thread then that can come across as spam. If you want to promote your content in a post, just make sure it's posted in a relevant sub.

It also never hurts to pm the mods and ask if it's okay to post your own blog.
Very good and makes sense. I appreciate the feedback and help.

I'd like to expand and say, don't post a link every time you write an article on your blog, as that is likely to get annoying pretty quickly. If anything, post the link once to inform people that it's something you're working on, and if other people like it enough, and it's relevant, they'll post the really good bits for you.

edit: a word

Content aggregation sites like this are designed for sharing the stuff you or others made. I don't see why posting links to stuff you created would be frowned upon by Voat, even if what you created is a blog about one thing or another. Just don't be awkward and pushy about it.

in addition to what @LegoMyEgo said (love that nick), my impression is that there is some internal deliberation going on at this time regarding spam and self-promotion - don't know if a consensus was reached, but it seems like it will be acceptable (or perhaps 'more' acceptable than it already is) to link to your own work, though i assume linking for profit will not be looked upon kindly
